etymologies.etymologyHTML: From aunt +‎ -ie.

definitions.definition: (Asia, Africa) Term of familiarity or respect for a middle-aged or elderly woman.
(LGBTQ, slang, US) An elderly gay man.[1]
To be or behave like the aunt of.

quote.citation: 1994, Maria Guadalupe Serna-Perez, Entrepreneurship, Women's Roles, and the Domestic Cycle:
quote.text: In the same melodrama, Madame Rotschild, a supporting character plays a similar role by "auntying" all children as a rich and powerful woman who can solve most problems in children's own homes.

quote.citation: 2003, Richard M. Lerner, Handbook of applied developmental science:
quote.text: More and more children are being "auntied" by women in the community who feel it is their duty as mothers to care for parentless children.
She had had only one unmitigated success in bending the girl to her will over the many years she'd auntied her: She had peeled the dialect right olf Lina's tongue.

quote.citation: 2019, Keturah Kendrick, No Thanks: Black, Female, and Living in the Martyr-Free Zone:
quote.text: “I am the best auntie of any auntie that has ever auntied,” she'd say, and in doing so reshape herself into the image her community needed to see.
